# The RT64 shaders the web page builds: one shader description a line, other mode L and H, color combiner L and H,
# flags, in hex. RT64 specializes each one's WGSL when the page is built and builds them with the game waiting: those
# above the first "section" line before the game starts, and a level's section when the level first draws with its
# shaders, so that nothing draws with the ubershader, which integrated graphics can't afford (N64Recomp-browser's
# docs/porting.md, Prebuilt shader lists).
#
# Recorded by code, not by playing: node lib/N64Recomp-browser/tools/record_shaders.mjs tools/shader_plan.json build/web
# roms/rayman2.us.z64 src/rt64_shaders.txt (its header says how), on tools/build_web.sh's page. Section 0 is the
# launcher, the boot (the logos, the attract demo, the title), the main menu and a new game's slot and name, reached
# with Start and A as a player does, and the intro story's first 10 s. Then the intro story (jail_10) for a minute, and
# a section a level of the game's table of levels, each reached from the intro story by tools/survey.js's go(), as the
# game's own exits change level, and walked about for 15 s of the game's time. The plan's last section, pause, goes
# into section 0: the pause menu (its Load and Options too), which comes up in any level and asks for its shaders a few
# at once, fewer than a section's build waits for, paused in learn_10, and the world map's (mapmonde) prompt to save
# the game and its answer. Not recorded: the levels past their starts, the bosses' fights and the game's other
# cutscenes. Flags follow settings (filtering, HDR, MSAA, upscaling), so a change to one of those defaults means
# recording again.
